title: Finite-codimensional separating ideals from finite residue extensions
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $R$ be a commutative unital Noetherian $K$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose $R/\mathfrak m$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ for every maximal proper ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Then $R/\mathfrak m^n$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ for every such $\mathfrak m$ and integer $n\ge1$, and $$\bigcap_{\mathfrak m\text{ maximal}}\ \bigcap_{n\ge1}\mathfrak m^n=(0).$$ The zero ring is allowed, with the intersection over an empty family interpreted as the whole zero ring. No reducedness, finite-type, localness, or Jacobson hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero), 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local), 00J0 (lemma-length-finite) and 00IY (lemma-dimension-is-length); finite maximal-power quotients and separation used to apply Kedlaya, Tate algebras, Corollary 11 after Proposition 10. Agent formulation of these consequences.

proof.text: Fix a maximal proper ideal $\mathfrak m$ and $n\ge1$. Choose lifts $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in R$ of a finite $K$-spanning list of $R/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. For each $0\le i<n$, choose ideal generators $g_{i1},\ldots,g_{it_i}$ of $\mathfrak m^i$, possible by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; for $i=0$ use $g_{01}=1$. Every $y\in\mathfrak m^i$ has the form $\sum_j r_jg_{ij}$. For each $j$, write $r_j=\sum_a c_{ja}b_a+u_j$ with $c_{ja}\in K$ and $u_j\in\mathfrak m$, by reducing $r_j$ modulo $\mathfrak m$. Therefore $y-\sum_{j,a}c_{ja}b_ag_{ij}=\sum_j u_jg_{ij}\in\mathfrak m^{i+1}$. Thus these finitely many $b_ag_{ij}$ span the $i$th successive quotient over $K$. This is an explicit coefficient reduction, requiring no assumption that $R$ itself is finite-dimensional over $K$.

source.place: Tag 00J0 (lemma-length-finite), proof: filtration by powers of the maximal ideal; Tag 00IY (lemma-dimension-is-length), finite generators modulo the maximal ideal. The K-spanning-list calculation is written out here.

proof.text: The classes of $b_ag_{ij}$ for $0\le i<n$ span $R/\mathfrak m^n$ over $K$. Indeed, for $r\in R$ begin with remainder $r_0=r\in\mathfrak m^0$. Applying step 1 to $r_i\in\mathfrak m^i$ gives a $K$-linear combination $v_i$ of the $b_ag_{ij}$ for that $i$ such that $r_{i+1}:=r_i-v_i\in\mathfrak m^{i+1}$. After the $n$ reductions, $r-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}v_i=r_n\in\mathfrak m^n$. The union of these $n$ finite lists is finite, so [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] gives the first conclusion. The base case $n=1$ is exactly the residue-space spanning assertion, and empty lists for zero powers cause no problem.

source.place: Tag 00J0 (lemma-length-finite), proof, finite filtration; explicit lifting of spanning lists in place of composition-length additivity.

proof.text: Let $x$ belong to all $\mathfrak m^n$ in the statement. For a fixed maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, put $N_{\mathfrak m}=\bigcap_{n\ge0}\mathfrak m^n R$; the additional $n=0$ term is $R$, so $x\in N_{\mathfrak m}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization] with $I=\mathfrak m$, $M=R$ (generated by $1$), and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$ (maximal proper ideals are prime: in $R/\mathfrak m$ every nonzero class generates the unit ideal and hence is a unit). It gives $f\notin\mathfrak m$ and an integer $e\ge0$ such that $f^ex=0$. In $R_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $f/1$ has inverse $1/f$, so multiplication by $1/f^e$ shows $x/1=0$. As this holds for every maximal ideal, [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-membership-at-maximal-localizations], applied with $J=(0)$ and $a=x$, gives $x=0$. Conversely zero belongs to every power, proving equality of the intersection with $(0)$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (1), based on Tag 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero); Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local), part (1), maximal-localization detection.

proof.text: If $R$ is the zero ring, there is no maximal proper ideal. The quotient assertion has no instances; the intersection over the empty family is $R=(0)$, as stipulated. Thus all conclusions also hold in this case.

source.place: Empty-family convention in the item; direct verification for the zero ring.

Steps 1-2: I checked the explicit K-spanning lists. Reducing r_j mod m leaves u_j in m, so u_j g_ij lies in m^{i+1}; the induction runs from r_0 = r through n reductions to r_n in m^n. Both steps are elementary and cite only the Noetherian and finite-dimensional definitions. Step 3: I checked 00IQ(1) (algebra.tex l.12257) against lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization with I = p = m and M = R (m is prime). It gives f not in m with f^e x = 0, so x/1 = 0 in R_m, and the 00HN node with J = 0 (Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal) gives x = 0. Step 4: the zero-ring convention is consistent. Edge cases: K, K[e]/e^2, KxK (a single m-adic intersection can be nonzero, the intersection over all maximal ideals is 0), K[t]; K(t)/K is correctly excluded by the hypothesis. An rg search found no duplicate. The citer lem-trf-affinoid-homomorphism-bounded uses exactly the two conclusions.
